title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) to evaluate whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The preregistered execution contract used shared_initial_generation (one initial model generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded conditions) to isolate repair-triggered differences from generator stochasticity. Under this contract we ran 200 paired tasks (50 per stratum: IOS-like vs JunOS-like × single-step vs multi-step) with declared model gpt-5-mini and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair attempt per task). All archived scoring artifacts show both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), yielding paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0, paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed archived), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not empirically computable. We reconcile these degenerate outcomes with respect to the preregistered contract, summarize the deterministic validator semantics used to define the primary outcome, provide explicit artifact pointers and representative hashes for reproducibility, and discuss construct/internal/external validity implications and targeted follow-ups supported by the archived artifacts.

sections.introduction: Automating intent-to-configuration translation accelerates NetOps but risks introducing unsafe device changes (reachability loss, policy violations, routing faults, or interface-state regressions). Tool-assisted mitigation typically follows a generate→validate→repair pattern: an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic sandbox verifier (Batfish-style) checks invariants, and the system either auto-repairs or escalates for human review. Prior prototypes and position papers recommend verifier-in-the-loop architectures and layered controls, but controlled, preregistered paired evidence that isolates the marginal benefit of a validator under a bounded repair budget is limited. We therefore asked the preregistered question: does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors compared to one-shot LLM generation when the initial generation is shared between arms so that any observed improvement must come from repair activity?
sections.related_work: Recent literature demonstrates active research on LLM-based NetOps and on verifier-augmented workflows. Intent-to-configuration translation and LLM-assisted configuration synthesis are explored by Nguyen Tu et al. (2024) and related ICNP/NetSoft works showing practical promise but reporting occasional unsafe outputs. Generate→validate→repair and bounded self-correction architectures are proposed and prototyped by several groups (e.g., Sang 2025; Okula 2026) and are echoed by survey and architecture papers that emphasize workflow-centred evaluation, human gates, and sandbox verification (Bilal et al. 2026; Malik 2026). Taxonomy and failure-mode analyses for agentic systems reinforce the need for layered defenses and auditability (Maharaj 2026; Vadlamudi 2026). These prior works motivate a confirmatory, preregistered, paired trial that fixes generator variance (shared_initial_generation) to reveal whether the verifier alone—operating with a bounded repair budget—produces measurable improvements in validator-detected errors.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand: We sealed CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 prior to execution (preregistration SHA256 aa4055d52c118741524c4c42d07efa977372be338b9bd96069dc7abfc5b32ac4). The single primary confirmatory estimand is the paired absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rate (guarded − baseline). Design and sampling: Confirmatory design is paired binary with 200 tasks (complete-pair policy). Tasks are balanced across 4 preregistered strata (50 tasks each): IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step (these stratum counts are preregistered and enforced; the authoritative task manifest is archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl, sha256 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b). Shared-initial-generation contract: to isolate repair-driven differences we used shared_initial_generation: a single LLM candidate per task was generated and reused by both baseline and guarded scoring episodes (preregistered initial_generation_calls_per_task=1). Model and adapters: declared model = gpt-5-mini per execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) and experiments used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family implementing a bounded generate→validate→repair transformation (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Validator semantics and failure-oracle: the primary harm oracle is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (a Batfish-like sandbox); the preregistered contamination_plan and validator checks include (explicitly) reachability/intra-VLAN connectivity tests, ACL/policy violations, routing-loop and path-consistency detection, and interface-state/workflow invariant checks (for example: ‘‘make-before-break’’ constraints and shutdown/configure/restore sequences). The validator produces per-episode fields validation_before/validation_after, normalized_configuration, violation_count, and violation_codes (examples of the validation fields and zero violation outputs appear in execution/scoring/*.json; representative hashes are provided below). Power and analysis plan: sample size n=200 was computed (target absolute reduction 10 percentage points, two-sided α=0.05, power=0.80 under McNemar discordant-pair assumptions; preregistration documents the calculation). Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes; 95% CI estimated by paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed archived). Missingness and sensitivity: predeclared complete-pair policy; sensitivity analysis treats failed calls conservatively if needed (documented in the preregistration). Reproducible artifacts: the experiment harness archive includes raw responses, per-episode validator traces, the full task manifest, and the execution manifest. Representative artifact pointers used in this paper: execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 9ec4eb2ce01f16d9eb0191b80eda199ec2655637aa2c6c775f8babb62962b46f), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c), analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951). The archive contains the full execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) and the canonicalized scoring records used as the authoritative reproducibility bundle.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: preregistered planned episodes = 400 (200 tasks × 2 conditions). Execution manifest reports completed_episodes = 400, failed_episodes = 0, and model_calls_used = 200 (consistent with shared_initial_generation; provider-call audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts={"shared_initial_generation":200}). Complete pairs: 200. Primary outcome—validator-clean counts: aggregated artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv) show baseline validator-clean = 200/200 (success rate 1.0) and guarded validator-clean = 200/200 (success rate 1.0). Paired contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200 (both-clean), n_10 = 0 (guarded-only-clean), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-clean), n_00 = 0 (both-error). Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed 1729) yielded 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Repair activity: the guarded adapter bounded to ≤1 repair per task invoked zero repairs (repair_count = 0). Therefore the preregistered secondary estimand repair_success_rate (fraction corrected after initial validator-detected error) is not computable from these results. Representative episodes: sample scoring records and validator traces for tasks pair-000001, pair-000002, and pair-000003 are archived; for example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256 b8ebf9546dabb93b06b15d40152e35a3e96a9d1c98cee131bb7f8065a8b6a2b4) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256 020baed3e0e4283cc5e25413af002166998bfc587a1919046ca53dab09251b30) contain the validator_trace objects that show normalized_configuration, validation_before/after and violation_count=0 for these episodes. Diagnostic statistics and consistency: deterministic_reconciliation and analysis logs confirm all deterministic accounting checks passed; no technical exclusions or missing pairs occurred. Because the observed data are degenerate (no discordant pairs), standard inferential machinery indicates no detectable marginal benefit under the executed contract (shared_init + bounded repair budget).
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded interpretation: the paired-null result has two concrete, artifact-backed readings. First, for every task the single shared initial candidate generated by gpt-5-mini satisfied the deterministic validator’s sandbox checks; the validator returned violation_count=0 for every episode in the canonical scoring records. Second, because no validator-detected errors occurred, the bounded repair loop never executed and therefore could not produce corrections. These outcomes are a direct consequence of the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract (intentionally suppressing generator variance) combined with the selected synthetic task bank and validator expressiveness. Experimental sensitivity and design trade-offs: the chosen contract isolates repair-mediated marginal effects by removing stochastic variability from repeated generation; this increases internal clarity at the cost of sensitivity to generator-sampling-induced failures. An independent_generation variant (one model call per condition) would increase the probability of initial-generator-induced discordance and therefore the empirical opportunity for repairs, but it conflates generator sampling variance with repair efficacy. Operational implications: whether a verifier materially improves outcomes in practice depends jointly on (1) the generator’s sampling dispersion (how often it proposes failing candidates in realistic usage), (2) the validator's fidelity relative to production device semantics (sandbox vs device-specific quirks), and (3) the repair policy (bounded single repair vs iterative repair with richer repair strategies). Our artifacts provide direct levers to explore these axes: the task manifest contains difficulty labels and required_sequences per task; the execution logs contain provider-call accounting; the validator traces contain explicit violation encodings when present. Follow-up experiments enabled by the archive include (a) switching to independent condition generation, (b) increasing the repair budget and applying iterative repair strategies, (c) substituting or extending the validator harm-oracle to model additional production semantics, and (d) introducing adversarial or crafted failure-inducing prompts.
sections.conclusion: We ran a sealed, preregistered paired trial to measure the marginal effect of a deterministic Batfish-style validator in a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline when generator variance is suppressed by shared_initial_generation. Under this contract and for the provided synthetic 200-task bank, both baseline and guarded arms were validator-clean on every task (200/200 each), producing a degenerate null (paired difference = 0.0; 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked, so repair-success could not be evaluated. These results do not contradict the potential utility of verifier-in-the-loop architectures; rather they highlight that preregistered contracts, task-bank challenge level, generator sampling policy, validator fidelity, and repair strategy jointly determine whether verifier assistance will produce observable gains. The archived artifacts (task manifest, raw responses, validator logs, paired contingency tables, and execution manifest) are sufficient to reproduce the run and to design follow-up preregistered comparisons that vary generation independence, repair budgeting, model families, validator expressiveness, and adversarial conditions.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-like sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

Preregistered shared_initial_generation (independent_condition_generation=false) produced exactly one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduces the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
